{"notes": "VISIT 5 (left 7:00). Nobody spoke while I was there, and I saw no one's hands on the table, so I have no new evidence about any individual. I don't know who placed which domino. I did not see the push or the result.

TABLE: Unchanged. The fish outline is complete and connected from START, with both tail tips reached. The 3 pale, disconnected dominoes near (23-24, 8.3-9) are still there, beside the upper tail line at the crossing. Nobody has taken responsibility for them. They may not break the chain, but I can't tell. Check after the push whether they mattered.

SOFIA: No new observations. Earlier: strong concept, plan and work split, and calm at 5:45. Gap: her 2:30 tail inspection either didn't happen or missed the strays. Ask her what she checked.

OMAR: No new observations. Clean handoff earlier. He offered at 2:30 to fix an off-side domino, but the strays remain and he said nothing about them. Ask whether those were the dominoes he meant, and why he didn't follow through.

HANA: No new observations. I've heard only one short 'hands off, here we go' from her. The belly section looks connected and clean, so her output is solid. Ask her directly about blockers and her role, and don't assume her quiet means disengaged.

JACK: No new observations. Positive, team-minded, and credited the team. He took on tilt and gap checking, but I never saw him do it and the strays survived. Ask what he actually checked. His execution evidence is thin.

REVIEW QUESTIONS: Who saw the strays? Why were they left? Who actually did the checking? Rate on what I saw and what they tell me, not on assumptions. Impact and collaboration are better supported than execution and ownership."}
